simple.meaning: סַבְתָּא (Çabtâʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “Sabta or Sabtah , the name of a son of Cush, and the country occupied by his posterity.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סַבְתָּא (H5454) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 10:7, with occurrences in Genesis, 1 Chronicles.

simple.summary: סַבְתָּא (Çabtâʼ) / H5454 is traced through Genesis 10:7, 1 Chronicles 1:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: Sabta or Sabtah , the name of a son of Cush, and the country occupied by his posterity
definitions.full: H5454. Sabta or Sabtah סַבְתָּא סַבְתָּה, proper name, of a people 3rd 'son' of Cush according to Gen 10:7 ( הָ֯ ), = 1Chr 1:9 ( אָ֯ ); identification with Σαββαθα [Periplus maris Erythr. 27 ], Σαυβαθα Ptol vi. 7, 38 , or Σαβατα [Strabo xvi. 42 ], Sabota [Plin NH vi. § 155, xii. 63 ], old commercial city of South Arabia, by Tu Ku, but this = Sabean שבות (not ׳ס ) Levy-Os ZMG xix (1865), 253 ; xx (1866), 273, compare Hal JAS 7, iv. 525 ; Glaser Skizze ii. 252 f. proposes Σαφθα (Ptol vi. 7, 30 ), near west shore of Persian Gulf; ᵐ5 Σαβαθα , Σαβατα , Σεβαθα . All uncertain conjectures.
definitions.rootNote: or סַבְתָּה ; probably of foreign derivation;

occurrences.englishText: The sons of Cush were: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were: Sheba and Dedan.
The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama, Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan.
